capabilities.title: Codebase structure
capabilities.requirement: escher's over-ceiling event handlers are split into named functions along their range and activation branches; escher's inline test modules leave document.rs while upstream's body stays; mcp.rs and schema.rs are split along their seams; every check stays green
capabilities.observed_gap: functions over the complexity ceiling went 74 → 80 → 83 across the last two epochs, the escher-authored growth in blitz-dom's event handlers (handle_click 74, handle_pointerdown 40, handle_key_or_input_event 56) and the range input's parse_float (19); the largest file, blitz-dom/src/document.rs, holds 2,793 code lines, 688 of them in five inline test modules; files over 800 code lines went 12 → 15 → 16, escher's own being escher-driver/src/mcp.rs (1,140) and schema.rs (840)

verification.acceptance: Read on the code audit's own instruments at the wrap of 2026-10-16-file-splits, in four parts. (1) `rust-code-analysis-cli` 0.0.25 through `escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme/evidence/complexity.py` over `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs`, `events/keyboard.rs` and `node/range.rs` prints `over-ceiling: handle_click handle_key_or_input_event handle_pointerdown handle_pointermove touch_action_pan_axes`. So `parse_float` and every extracted range and activation function stand at or under the ceiling, and the three parents stand below their pre-split figures at their upstream-floor remainder (the reading accepted at that chunk's P5 review). (2) escher's inline test modules `changed_set_tests` and `font_reading_tests` are gone from `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`, now `#[cfg(test)] #[path]` children in sibling files, and the file's lines 1–3461 (upstream's body and its four test modules) equal the base `4f3939914e525e284a32beb91bdc97972d40c904` byte for byte. (3) `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs` is split along its seams into `mcp/framing.rs`, `mcp/listing.rs` and `mcp/result.rs`, with its tests in `mcp_tests.rs`. `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` is split into its table and `schema/spec.rs` (the shape types), with its tests in `schema_tests.rs`. Every one of these files and the two parents is at or under 800 tokei code lines. (4) Every existing check stays green: `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast`, `doc` and `a11y` pass, and the CI run on the pushed sha reads `verdict: green`, every check succeeded, `Stand checks repeated` and `Coverage report` included.

capabilities.notes:
2026-10-16 (2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme, phase P5): not claimed — not provable by this chunk alone. Its acceptance has legs in two working-route entries: the handler splits (this chunk: escher's range and activation arms as named functions, `parse_float` in steps) and "File splits" (`document.rs`'s inline test modules, `mcp.rs` and `schema.rs`), which names v020-01 too (escher-0.2.0/working-route.md:13). The cap stays pooled for "File splits". Measured at take-up with the audit's instrument (`rust-code-analysis-cli` 0.0.25): upstream's own bodies of the three handlers read `handle_click` 69 · `handle_pointerdown` 35 · `handle_key_or_input_event` 50 at the merge base `434e0661`, against 74 · 40 · 56 at HEAD. So "escher's handler branches no longer over the ceiling" is read on escher's code — the extracted functions and the `parse_float` steps at or under 15, the parents below their HEAD figures with the upstream figure as their floor — accepted by the operator at the P5 review (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-16T14-07-11-phase/p5-card-1.md`).

2026-10-16 (2026-10-16-file-splits, phase P5): claimed by this chunk, which takes both legs. The handler-splits leg shipped in 2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme and is re-read here by that chunk's own complexity gate, byte-equal. The file-splits leg is this chunk's: the two escher test modules out of `document.rs`, and `mcp.rs` and `schema.rs` split along their seams, the shape on the operator's P4 fork answer «Seams + tests file». The acceptance was concretized at the P5 review (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-16T15-51-04-phase/p5-card-1.md`), and the operator approved it with «yes». At take-up the audit's five-module figure for `document.rs` read six modules, two of them escher's; `schema.rs` has no help-text seam, its seam being the shape types.

capabilities.title: Fast-failing mutants
capabilities.requirement: each of the six mutants caught only by the timeout fails a test fast, and the mutation score holds at 0 survivors
capabilities.observed_gap: six mutants are caught only by the 300 s timeout, never by a failing test: three in TimerTicks::next, two in mcp.rs read_request, one in MutationWriter::create_text_node

verification.acceptance: A mutation run over the units that held the six timeout-only mutants catches each of them with a failing test well inside the timeout, and the run's score holds at 0 survivors.

capabilities.title: Engine debts dispositioned
capabilities.requirement: each recorded engine debt reaches the founder as a fork, then is fixed and proven on the stand or a fixture with its upstream merge surface owned, pinned as a stated limit, or kept as a residual by his word
capabilities.observed_gap: the engine ignores inert; it does not read aria-checked, nor follow aria-activedescendant to the current option; Node::absolute_position reads a self-scrolled box shifted by its own scroll; the hit does not stop at a contain: paint box; a clicked caret in a password field reveals the hidden characters' width class (measured: index 5 against 2); disabled removes focusability on any element, not only form controls; a transformed box's client rect reads its untransformed position; covered is ambiguous on a zero-height box

verification.acceptance: Each of the nine recorded engine debts carries the founder's recorded answer, and its outcome matches that answer: a fixed debt is proven by a check on the stand or a fixture in both layout modes, with an owner named for its upstream merge surface; a pinned debt has its limit stated and a check that holds it; a kept debt stands as a residual line.

capabilities.title: Trace to regression check
capabilities.requirement: any driver session, through the CLI or MCP, is recorded as a replayable check, ordinary test input that runs in CI, failing when the UI's behaviour changes and passing while it holds
capabilities.observed_gap: the cold-agent pipe replays one agent-written JSON check on a fresh session with no model; no general command turns a driver session into a check

verification.acceptance: A stand session driven through the command line and one driven through MCP are each recorded and replayed as ordinary tests in CI; each replay passes on the unchanged app and fails when the app's behaviour is changed under it, with no hand edit of the recording.

capabilities.title: Visual lint
capabilities.requirement: one command reports, for the current screen, each element that overlaps another, is clipped, has truncated text, lies off-screen, has zero size or fails text contrast, naming its stable id and measured reason
capabilities.observed_gap: covered and off-screen are named per action only; text contrast is checked on the stand by one test, not by a command

verification.acceptance: On a fixture that plants each of the six defects, one lint command names every planted element by its stable id with its measured reason, and on the stand at boot it reports no defect the stand's recorded contrast and layout readings do not hold.

capabilities.title: One virtual clock
capabilities.requirement: every time the engine and the app read in a headless run comes from one virtual clock only the driver moves; two shots of the same state read the same pixels
capabilities.observed_gap: time under a driver session moves only by advance, but the overlay scrollbar fade reads the wall clock, so two screenshots within 0.7 s of a scroll can differ

verification.acceptance: In a headless run that paints overlay scrollbars, two screenshots of the same state taken right after a scroll, with wall time passing between them and no driver advance, read the same pixels, and the fade moves only when the driver advances time.

capabilities.title: Load wait
capabilities.requirement: a command that meets a load in flight waits it out within a stated bound, proven on a fixture
capabilities.observed_gap: no command waits out a network load: a command that finds a load in flight reports it and returns, so an app that loads over the network is polled by its caller

verification.acceptance: On a fixture whose load completes inside the stated bound, an acting command returns settled with the loaded content on screen; on one whose load does not complete, the command returns within the bound and says the load is still in flight.

capabilities.title: Select by id
capabilities.requirement: a select is driven by id like any control and read in the snapshot, proven on a fixture
capabilities.observed_gap: there is no select interaction model

verification.acceptance: On a fixture holding a select, an agent chooses an option by the control's stable id through the driver, and the snapshot reads the select with its role, its name and the chosen value, the focus order unchanged.

capabilities.title: Large screen in parts
capabilities.requirement: a screen over the snapshot text budget is read in parts an agent can walk, proven on a fixture
capabilities.observed_gap: a screen over the 10,000-byte snapshot budget (Cells) cannot be read whole

verification.acceptance: On a fixture whose screen exceeds the 10,000-byte snapshot budget, an agent reads it part by part, each part within the budget, and the parts together hold every node of the whole screen exactly once.

capabilities.title: Capabilities stated for a consumer
capabilities.requirement: what escher can do, and its stated limits, is written where Viola's frontend planning reads it, before that planning starts

verification.acceptance: Before Viola's frontend planning starts, the operator confirms one statement of what escher can do and its stated limits, current with 0.2.0's capabilities, stands where that planning reads it.

capabilities.title: Cold-agent bar
capabilities.requirement: 0.2.0 ends with a cold-agent run over its new capabilities, judged against a wrong-call bar the founder sets from 0.1.0's baseline of 0 wrong in 43
capabilities.observed_gap: 0.1.0's run is the baseline: 4 tasks, 43 calls, 0 wrong, $0.32; the bar starts in 0.2.0

verification.acceptance: A fresh agent given only the tool exercises 0.2.0's new capabilities in one recorded run whose wrong-call count meets the bar the founder set from 0.1.0's baseline, and the check it writes passes on replay.
